pairs.subject: health-checks
pairs.evidence: examples/hirelane/design/check-contrast.mjs:268 The contrast checker collapses unreadable inputs and measured violations into one failure result, preventing consumers from distinguishing unverifiable checks from confirmed failures.

techniques.evidence: examples/hirelane/package.json:11 An explicit command launches fresh checks on demand; these scripts do not couple observation to UI rendering.

examples/hirelane/design/check-contrast.mjs:268 Individual diagnostics identify affected members, but the aggregate boolean merges MODEL/UNREAD outcomes with confirmed UNDER violations and provides no distinct undetermined summary.

examples/hirelane/design/check-contrast.mjs:160 These standalone source scans read fresh files per invocation; there is no cached verdict shared among health surfaces whose TTL or invalidation requires judgment.

examples/hirelane/design/check-contrast.mjs:265 This below-floor instruction also follows MODEL/UNREAD failures, which need checker-specific remediation; check definitions do not structurally declare fixability.

examples/hirelane/design/check-contrast.mjs:240 The diagnostic admits that measurement could not run, but immediately sets the same failed boolean used for measured violations instead of producing a first-class unverifiable outcome.

pairs.registryProposal: Clarify which lifecycle requirements apply to standalone static checkers: three-state-outcomes explicitly includes lint and compliance sweeps, while caching and probe lifecycle requirements primarily describe shared dependency probes.
